correctness.rationale: Derivation from the exact expected message-preference kernel is algebraic. A strictly increasing log-odds quotient K has range (3,infinity), giving the unique separatrix pair for 2<beta<5/2 and proving all other regimes. A continuous increasing interval map yields monotone convergence within each fixed-point interval. Endpoint expansions, derivative and critical cubic verify stability including boundaries; Taylor inversion proves the square-root collision. Hyperbolicity and uniform endpoint control prove the source-imbalance persistence. SymPy/mpmath checks pass 2797 assertions; finite checks do not replace the proof.

evidence: Mao et al. impose strictly positive source weights and a contraction condition ||W||+2gamma<1; under their condition the equilibrium is unique.

Xia et al. use nonlinear power-weighted neighbor assimilation and distinguish strong/weak biases and network-dependent polarization; their update has different numerator and denominator from the two-message preference quotient.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The contraction theorem does not dominate the three-attractor regime: its kernel and hypotheses differ and its uniqueness conclusion would exclude the five fixed points. The equal-opposing-neighbor biased-assimilation reduction has an additive self-opinion term not present in the message-preference map, so its equilibrium types do not imply the 2 and 5/2 thresholds. A more general conjugacy from uninspected literature remains possible.

value.rationale: The binary opposite-message law is a natural model of conflicting information sources. In the exact nonlinear source-preference mechanism the result rigorously separates unique interior moderation (beta<=2), coexistence of moderation and both extremes (2<beta<5/2), and two-sided extremization (beta>=5/2). Exact basin boundaries, their nontrivial square-root collision and persistence under source imbalance make this a useful phase classification rather than a routine reparameterization or an isolated computation.
